devotionals.word:
Welcome. This is day one of a year of mornings, and the first thing we do is not very impressive. We gather. We read slowly and let the book say what it actually says, before we make it say anything else.

Gather is the move of humility, and Proverbs puts it plainly. The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge. Fear there doesn't mean being scared of a bully. It means the posture you take when you know you are not the smartest person in the room. You show up to learn, not to correct.

That is hard for most of us. We read a verse and immediately want to explain it, apply it, defend it, post it. Gather says hold on. First, just look at the words. What does it actually say? Not what it reminds you of. Not what you have always heard. What is on the page. Timothy calls it rightly handling the word of truth, and a worker who does that has nothing to be ashamed of.

This year you'll move through seven ways of reading: Gather, Filter, Deliver, Count, Shape, Flow, Zoom. Each one carries a virtue. They all start right here, with the slow, humble work of reading what is actually in front of you.
devotionals.apply: Today, before anything else, read the two verses above out loud, once, slowly. Don't explain them. Just hear them. That's the whole move.
devotionals.prayer: Lord, quiet me down. Help me come to your word today not to use it but to hear it. Teach me to begin at the beginning, with humility.

devotionals.word:
Welcome to the year. This is the first morning of a long, slow walk through the whole Bible, and we're doing it with a method called the Seven Moves. You don't need to memorize them today. You just need to meet them. Each move is a way of paying attention, and each one carries a virtue. Gather is humility. Filter is discernment. Deliver is generosity. Count is honesty. Shape is clarity. Flow is patience. Zoom is perspective. Seven moves for seven days, and we'll keep that rhythm all year.

Today's move is Gather. Gather means read what's actually there, before you decide what it means. Not what you remember it saying. Not what a sermon told you it says. What it says. It sounds simple and it isn't, because most of us open the book already sure of the point. Gather says slow down and let the words have their say first. That's why the virtue is humility. You can't gather anything while you're still talking.

Proverbs opens with a list of what these words are for: wisdom, instruction, insight, prudence, discretion. Then it stops and names the starting line. The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge. Not the end of it. The beginning. The first move in learning anything real is to remember you aren't the one who set the table. You're the one being fed.

That's the whole first week in one idea. It's also why Paul tells Timothy to handle the word rightly. You can't handle what you haven't first picked up.
devotionals.apply: Today, before you read anything else, try this. Open to Proverbs 1 and read verses one through seven out loud, slowly, once. Don't highlight. Don't take notes. Just notice one phrase you'd normally skip over. Sit with that phrase for a minute and ask what it actually says, before you add anything to it.
devotionals.prayer: Lord, teach me to gather before I speak. Give me a humble heart that listens to your words as they are, not as I want them to be. Start me well today, and walk with me through the whole year. Amen.

readings.text: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge; fools despise wisdom and instruction.
Do your best to present yourself to God as one approved, a worker who has no need to be ashamed, rightly handling the word of truth.

devotionals.word:
The first move is not to analyze or argue or apply. It's to gather. Take in what the text actually says before you decide what it means.

That sounds simple, and it isn't. Most of us read to confirm what we already believe. We come to the page with our minds made up and scan for agreement. Gathering is the discipline of setting that down and letting the words speak first.

The wisdom books call this the beginning, not the end. The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge. "Fear" here doesn't mean terror. It means the humility that says I don't already know this, and I'm willing to be taught. A fool, Proverbs says, despises instruction. The wise person starts by receiving.

Paul makes the same point with a different picture. A worker rightly handling the word of truth. You can't rightly handle something you haven't first picked up and looked at honestly. Careful handling comes first. Read slowly. Notice what is there. Refuse to skip the parts that make you uncomfortable.

So before you study anything this year, practice the first move. Read it once, slowly, and just notice what it says. Not what it means, not whether you agree. What it says. That's the whole of Gather. The rest of the method is built on nothing else.
devotionals.apply: Open to any passage. The one above will do. Read it twice. The first time, don't try to learn anything. Just name the plain facts of the sentence in your own words: who, what, where, when. Notice what you usually skip.
devotionals.prayer: Lord, teach me to be a receiver before I'm a critic. Slow me down. Give me the humility to let your words speak before I speak. Amen.
